criteria.text: Identifies the mismatch between English law / English courts in the SPA and New York law / New York arbitration in the escrow agreement, and the risk of parallel proceedings on escrow claims.

Identifies that the board approval was given at a meeting with only 2 directors present when Article 11 requires a quorum of three, so the approval may be invalid, and recommends a fresh or ratifying resolution.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Calculates the long-stop date as 9 July 2027 (150 days after signing on 9 February 2027) and identifies that expected clearance on 23 July 2027 falls after it, recommending an extension.

Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 45-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.
Gives the long-stop period as 150 days and as the date 9 July 2027, with days remaining from 18 February 2027 (141 days).
Opens with a short 'Bottom line' / executive summary stating the overall conclusion and the most important risks before the detailed analysis.
Checks whether computed deadlines fall on a weekend and adjusts them under the documents' Business Day definition.
